home.heroSubtitle: Mangala Shri Bhuti Japan offers Tibetan Buddhist teachings and meditation practice in Japanese.
home.rinpocheQuote: “In the end, all teachings—traditional or informal—have one aim: to help reduce self-importance and make room for the truth.”
home.weeklyDharmaQuote: "Do not always focus on fixing situations externally and thereby distract yourself from what is happening internally. If you go inward, no matter how challenging it may seem, you are going to become victorious."
home.donateDesc: The activities of Mangala Shri Bhuti Japan are sustained by your generous donations.
home.newsletterDesc: Receive event information and the latest news by email.
home.programsQuote: “Together, this culture of study, practice and service molds students into people who are, if it could be said in a word, more selfless than when they entered the path.”
home.programsIntro: The path we follow in Mangala Shri Bhuti culminates in the teachings on Dzogchen, which are only transmitted and practiced in retreat. All students orient their study and practice toward eventually receiving these teachings directly from Kongtrul Rinpoche, undertaking a progression of practices and mind training along with a comprehensive course of study. Service is also highly emphasized as an aspect of students' development and is a central ethos of our organization.

lifeRelease.title: Life Release
lifeRelease.description: The practice of life release (tsethar) is a compassionate activity of freeing animals destined for slaughter.
lifeRelease.whatIsDesc: Life release (tsethar in Tibetan) is a traditional Buddhist practice of saving and releasing animals that would otherwise be killed. It is considered a powerful practice for generating merit and cultivating compassion.

programs.title: Programs
programs.quote: “Together, this culture of study, practice and service molds students into people who are, if it could be said in a word, more selfless than when they entered the path.”
programs.intro: In Mangala Shri Bhuti, students learn through a variety of study courses while practicing Lojong (mind training) and a progression of practices, walking a path that culminates in the teachings on Dzogchen, transmitted only in retreat. Service to the sangha is likewise an essential element in developing one's own qualities. Together, this culture of study, practice and service molds students into people who are, if it could be said in a word, more selfless than when they entered the path.
annualTeachingText: Once a year, we hold a teaching gathering led by either Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche or Dungse Jampal Norbu.
We also hold the Nyingma Summer Seminar in Japan each year, in parallel with the U.S. program (recorded, with simultaneous Japanese interpretation).
programs.studyGroupText: We hold a monthly study group at Tashi Gachil in Kameoka, Kyoto. Its aim is to move beyond a purely conceptual understanding of the teachings, deepening our understanding through experience in daily life, and providing a space to share what we discover personally and inspire one another. Anyone interested in working with their mind is welcome to join, whether or not they are already interested in Buddhism.
programs.retreatText: In the busyness of modern life, it has become difficult to find long stretches of time to sit and look inward. To address this, we hold a monthly one-day meditation retreat (five one-hour sitting sessions) in a quiet, green setting in Kameoka City. Many participants find that after sitting for an extended period, they carry a strength of mind that is less easily swept away by habitual reactions, even after the retreat ends. Anyone interested in meditation is welcome, and partial attendance for even a single session is also accepted.
onlineCourseText: How can we bring the teachings into daily life? How can everyday experience nourish us along the path? How can we then progress through the stages of the Buddhist path, become a student under a single teacher, and continue Vajrayana teachings and practice while living an ordinary life? As one way of meeting these heartfelt questions, Mangala Shri Bhuti offers an Online Lineage Course.

Held over Zoom so that participants can join regardless of location, the Online Lineage Course draws on Kongtrul Rinpoche's teachings from around the world, selecting and organizing material suited to each theme as the basis for study, contemplation, and meditation. Sessions are held online every two weeks, giving participants a chance to share their experiences and insights with one another and deepen their understanding together.
programs.tsokText: Twice a month, we hold a tsok (feast offering) practice at Tashi Gachil in Kameoka City. Open only to those who have received empowerment from Rinpoche.
programs.lifeReleaseText: Once a year, together with Kongtrul Rinpoche or Dungse Jampal Norbu, we hold a life-release ceremony (tsetar) in the sea off Minami-Izu, releasing fish and other sea creatures back into the wild. For those unable to attend in person, we accept donations toward this practice. (Life release is a ceremony in which captured creatures are released into a pond or the wild as an act of merit.) Please see the schedule page for the exact date.
